Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing, particularly Articles 3, 4, 7, 8, 12, 14, 17 and 18; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving the implementing regulation of Law 10/2010; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July establishing the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership; Royal Decree 1021/2015 of 13 November on automatic exchange of financial-account information; Royal Decree-Law 7/2021 of 27 April implementing EU AML and tax-transparency measures; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended; EU Regulation 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds; and applicable Spanish commercial-register and accounting legislation.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must have a registered office in Spain under Article 9 of the Companies Act, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010. The registered office must correspond to the place where the company has its effective administrative and management center or its principal establishment or operation. A serviced or virtual office may be used for registered-office and correspondence purposes if the provider lawfully accepts official notices and the address is genuine and accessible. It is not sufficient as the sole operational arrangement for wholesale distribution of clinical diagnostic ELISA assays and reagents. The business should maintain documented warehouse, logistics, quality, product-traceability, responsible-person, and customer-support arrangements appropriate to the products. IVD products must comply with Regulation (EU) 2017/746 on in vitro diagnostic medical devices, including applicable operator-registration, conformity, traceability, vigilance, storage, labeling, and distribution obligations. Spanish-language regulatory documentation and, where applicable, AEMPS or regional health-authority requirements must be reviewed before trading.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central for name certification; the competent Provincial Mercantile Registry of the registered office address for statutory inscription.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), notably Articles 20-23, 33-39, 61-62 and 100 for Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada formation; Commercial Registry Regulations approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public incorporation deed (escritura pública de constitución) submitted for inscription through the electronic case file of the Provincial Mercantile Registry.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 39 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

An SL must maintain minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation. The paid-up capital must be evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit issued by a Spanish credit institution; the certificate must refer to the company in formation and be attached to the notarial deed.

Funding & unlock path: Fire-safety technical certificate and first-occupancy licence from the municipal authority; structural soundness and site-suitability certificate issued by a competent architect or engineer; workplace-risk-prevention plan and emergency procedures approved under Law 31/1995 and Royal Decree 393/2007 on self-protection measures if required by the activity category.

Paid-in capital rule: An SL must maintain minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation. The paid-up capital must be evidenced by a bank certificate of deposit issued by a Spanish credit institution; the certificate must refer to the company in formation and be attached to the notarial deed.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The shareholders of ES_SL, acting as the founding general meeting, RESOLVE: (i) to incorporate ES_SL as a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada under the Capital Companies Act; (ii) to approve the articles and Bylaws annexed; (iii) to subscribe the entire share capital of EUR 3,000, divided into 3,000 equal participations of EUR 1 each, fully paid by bank deposit; (iv) to fix the registered office at Calle Mayor 12, 28013 Madrid, Spain; (v) to appoint [Full Name] as sole director (Administrador Único) for an indefinite term; and (vi) to authorize the execution of the public deed, obtain the provisional tax number, register the company in the Mercantile Registry, publish the announcement, and complete all ancillary formalities.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS); municipal industrial and licensing department of the competent Ayuntamiento; Consejería de Industria and Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the Autonomous Community

Category: Municipal opening and operation license for wholesale warehouse distribution of IVD reagents (licencia de apertura y funcionamiento) and registration of the establishment before AEMPS as a distributor of in-vitro diagnostic medical devices under Regulation (EU) 2017/746

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Central Electronic Portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

A non-resident entity intending to carry out taxable activities in Spain must appoint a fiscal representative if established outside the EU/EEA and submit Form 036 (censo de empresarios) or Form 030 to the competent AEAT office using a recognised digital certificate to obtain a Spanish NIF (for non-resident legal entities, the NIF carries the 'W' prefix) and, where applicable, a VAT identification number (NIF-IVA) linked to the permanent establishment. A resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada receives a provisional NIF at the time of incorporation before the public deed, which is confirmed after registration in the Mercantile Registry; the company must then file Form 036 to complete census registration and to declare commencement of activities, with VAT registration activated on the same form prior to issuing its first invoice.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — the resident SL is a separate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax) on worldwide income at a 25% general headline rate (15% reduced rate available for newly created trading companies in the first two tax years under Article 29.1 LIS); Spain does not recognise pass-through classification for a limited liability company, and the territorial scope applies only to non-resident entities without a permanent establishment. — A non-resident entity intending to carry out taxable activities in Spain must appoint a fiscal representative if established outside the EU/EEA and submit Form 036 (censo de empresarios) or Form 030 to the competent AEAT office using a recognised digital certificate to obtain a Spanish NIF (for non-resident legal entities, the NIF carries the 'W' prefix) and, where applicable, a VAT identification number (NIF-IVA) linked to the permanent establishment. A resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada receives a provisional NIF at the time of incorporation before the public deed, which is confirmed after registration in the Mercantile Registry; the company must then file Form 036 to complete census registration and to declare commencement of activities, with VAT registration activated on the same form prior to issuing its first invoice.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation — the resident SL is a separate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax) on worldwide income at a 25% general headline rate (15% reduced rate available for newly created trading companies in the first two tax years under Article 29.1 LIS); Spain does not recognise pass-through classification for a limited liability company, and the territorial scope applies only to non-resident entities without a permanent establishment.

Available election forms

No US-style check-the-box or free-form classification election exists under Spanish law. Available statutory elections include: (i) the consolidated tax group regime for Spanish groups under Articles 62–70 LIS, requiring at least 75% shareholding or voting rights, elected by filing Form 036 and binding for a minimum period; (ii) the optional SOCIMI (listed REIT) regime under Ley 11/2009, elected through AEAT notification and subject to compulsory dividend distribution rules; (iii) the patent box reduced tax rate under Article 23 LIS, requiring a formal election per qualifying intangible asset and documentation of the substance; (iv) the group VAT registration election under Article 84.2 LIVA for corporate groups. European anti-tax-avoidance (ATAD) hybrid mismatch rules are applied automatically via RDL 4/2021 and do not permit elective deviation, although entities may be designated as reverse hybrids in prescribed circumstances.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general turnover exemption threshold applies to resident taxable persons; VAT registration is mandatory before commencement of any taxable supply in Spain through Form 036/037. For intra-EU B2C distance sales by an EU-established supplier, Spain applies the EU-wide €10,000 annual threshold, below which VAT is chargeable in the supplier's Member State; for non-established foreign suppliers, an activity-based nexus triggers registration without any monetary de minimis threshold, subject to the special OSS/IOSS regimes where applicable.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Zero rating (exemption with right to deduction) applies to: (i) exports of physical goods to non-EU destinations under Article 21 LIVA, provided the goods physically leave Spanish/EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch (extendable on justification); (ii) intra-EU B2B supplies under Article 25 LIVA where the customer communicates a valid EU VAT number, the goods are transported to another Member State, and the supplier files Intrastat returns where applicable; (iii) international transport and ancillary services, and services directly related to exported goods or otherwise falling under Articles 69 and 70 LIVA, including certain offshore services where the place of supply is deemed to be outside the EU. The exporter must hold commercial and transport documentation evidencing the border-crossing and receipt by the foreign customer; for wholesale distribution of IVD diagnostic reagents, the zero-rating claim must be supported by a customs-validated export declaration together with the international sales contract and transport evidence.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA — Single Administrative Document) with exit confirmation from the customs office
  • Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport contract showing arrival at the foreign destination
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer/statement evidencing collection of export proceeds in EUR or foreign currency
  • Commercial invoice and international sales contract with Incoterms 2020 terms
  • AEAT export certificate or Exit Summary Declaration (EXS) confirmation and any Pre-Exit Notification
  • Intrastat declaration and printout of the customer's VIES VAT validation for intra-EU supplies
  • Proof of Expedition for Intra-Community Deliveries (PEM) where the goods move directly to another EU Member State

Spain does not operate a real-time pre-clearance fiscal stamping system. Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing is phased under Ley 28/2022 (Crea y Crece) and Royal Decree 1007/2023: taxpayers with turnover above €8 million must issue and receive structured electronic invoices from 2026, and all other businesses from 2027, through interoperable platforms connecting to AEAT. Large taxpayers (turnover above €6 million), VAT groups, and taxpayers included in the Immediate Supply of Information (Suministro Inmediato de Información, SII) regime must transmit invoice registers to AEAT electronically within four business days using machine-readable formats. The Veri*factu regulation requires all billing software to be certified, ensuring that invoices are traceable and contain a unique QR or hash identifier; regional masks such as TicketBAI in the Basque Country and Navarra impose additional digital signature and transmission duties in those territories.

AEAT may retrospectively review export zero-rating claims within the general four-year VAT limitation period (ten years for unreported transactions). Where the zero-rating is wrongly claimed or documentation is incomplete, late, or contradictory, AEAT assesses VAT at the 21% rate plus late-payment interest and imposes graduated administrative penalties under Articles 191–201 of the Ley General Tributaria, ranging from 50% to 150% of the assessed amount depending on the existence of concealment or incorrect data. Deliberate evasion exceeding €120,000 in one tax year constitutes a criminal offence under Article 305 of the Código Penal, punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and fines of two to six times the defrauded amount. False export declarations may also trigger the smuggling regime of Ley 12/1995 and the denial or clawback of input VAT credits previously attributed to the zero-rated export transaction.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain is a euro-area member with full capital-account and current-account convertibility under Articles 63-66 TFEU; no prior exchange-control authorization is required for inbound equity, trade settlements, dividends, or loan repayments. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to taxation rather than FX controls: outbound dividends from an SL to a non-resident parent are exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if qualifying, or subject to a 19% domestic withholding tax reduced by DTT (e.g., 5% under US-Spain, 10% under most LATAM treaties, 0% intra-EU with 5% holding requirement). Non-resident investors must file post-closing statistical declarations with the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores; there is no monetary conversion gate on EUR receipts or payments.

Export proceeds surrender rules

None. Spain imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no repatriation threshold, and no forced conversion ratio. Exporters may retain currency in any authorized bank account; however, an invoiced export of IVD reagents benefiting from export financing must be route-repatriated under documentary evidence (shipping documents, customs SAD, and SWIFT MT103 proof) within standard commercial credit terms to avoid balance-of-payments misstatement. All international transactions must be reported in the Banco de España quarterly balance-of-payments survey (declaración de operaciones con el exterior) when aggregated movements exceed EUR 50,000 per counterparty per year.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks (ESCB); exchange-control and balance-of-payments surveillance jointly with the Dirección General del Tesoro y Política Financiera (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise) for the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores (Foreign Investment Registry).

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Wise Fit: High

Feasibility: MEDIUM for a Spanish SL in IVD reagent wholesale; PSD2-licensed European e-money institutions (e.g., Wise Business, Qonto, Ramp Network equivalent) may be opened remotely for ancillary payments and multi-currency currency access without a Spanish branch under EEA passporting. Legal constraint: EMIs cannot provide credit, LC operations, or margin FX; inbound payments from LATAM distributors are subject to heightened AML false-positives in the healthcare sector, so the EMI ledger must not be used as the sole collection vehicle; SEPA accountability and the SL's NIF-linked bank account validation still require a traditional deposit-taking entity for capital escrow and treasury concentration.

Ramp Fit: High

Feasibility: MEDIUM for a Spanish SL in IVD reagent wholesale; PSD2-licensed European e-money institutions (e.g., Wise Business, Qonto, Ramp Network equivalent) may be opened remotely for ancillary payments and multi-currency currency access without a Spanish branch under EEA passporting. Legal constraint: EMIs cannot provide credit, LC operations, or margin FX; inbound payments from LATAM distributors are subject to heightened AML false-positives in the healthcare sector, so the EMI ledger must not be used as the sole collection vehicle; SEPA accountability and the SL's NIF-linked bank account validation still require a traditional deposit-taking entity for capital escrow and treasury concentration.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Healthcare-sector concentration: IVD reagents classified as medical products subject to AEMPS (Spanish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency) distribution licensing; concern over unauthorized pharmaceutical-like traffic.

Root cause: Healthcare-sector concentration: IVD reagents classified as medical products subject to AEMPS (Spanish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency) distribution licensing; concern over unauthorized pharmaceutical-like traffic.

Defense evidence: AEMPS establishment registration certificate (Comunicación de Puesta en el Mercado), CE IVDR/IVD Directive 98/79/EC certificates for principal products, ISO 13485 quality-system certificate, distribution agreements with EU manufacturers, and a matrix of end-customer clinical laboratories to evidence legitimate supply-chain provenance.
Non-resident capital injection from a LATAM or holding-company jurisdiction linked to a Panama/Chile/Turkey parent, triggering higher jurisdictional risk scoring.

Root cause: Non-resident capital injection from a LATAM or holding-company jurisdiction linked to a Panama/Chile/Turkey parent, triggering higher jurisdictional risk scoring.

Defense evidence: Certificate of incorporation and registry extract of the parent with legalized chain of title, audited financial statements of the shareholder, proof of direct foreign investment filing to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores, tax-residency certificate, and a notarized corporate resolution authorizing the equity transfer into the Spanish SL.
Screening hit on the UBO in due-diligence databases due to name similarity or prior PEP exposure in a healthcare procurement context.

Root cause: Screening hit on the UBO in due-diligence databases due to name similarity or prior PEP exposure in a healthcare procurement context.

Defense evidence: Official identity document and NIE, negative PEP/PEP-sanctions search from a top-tier KYC provider (Thomson Reuters/World-Check), sworn statement of legitimate business intent, and a bank-account-attorney letter (carta de referencia previa) from the UBO's home-country prime bank.
Inbound wire from a LATAM distributor (e.g., a Mexican or Chilean laboratory) flagged under OFAC/EU sanctions screening for a shared-name counterparty.

Root cause: Inbound wire from a LATAM distributor (e.g., a Mexican or Chilean laboratory) flagged under OFAC/EU sanctions screening for a shared-name counterparty.

Defense evidence: Executed distribution and proforma sales contracts, final commercial invoice and packing list, laboratory purchase order, customs airway/CBL customs declaration showing Spanish HS code 3822/3002, and a sanctions screen report confirming no match to prohibited persons.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant protocol: equity injection from a non-resident shareholder executed via SWIFT MT103 (CHIPS/Fedwire fallback) or SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated round-trip from the investor's own bank; remittance field 70 must state 'APORTACIÓN DE CAPITAL SOCIAL - ES_SL - INVERSIÓN EXTERIOR' and the SWIFT field 72/77B must identify the investor name, NIF/NIE, and the reference to the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores post-investment declaration (modelo DP-2 Consolidado, within 30 days for non-EU investors). Verification steps: (1) pre-deposit into the Capital Escrow Account named after the SL in a Spanish bank, (2) notarial deed of increase of capital or constitution referencing the deposit certificate, (3) disbursement of the escrowed funds to the SL's operational account only after certificate of deposit registration at the Commercial Registry, and (4) filing of the Bank of Spain balance-of-payments statistical form whenever the single receipt exceeds EUR 50,000. All funds must destine to a Spanish IBAN ESG followed by BBVA/Santander bank code.Primary rails: (1) SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) for intra-EEA suppliers of reagents and consumables under standard 24-72 hours execution; (2) SWIFT MT103 (bank-to-bank TT) for USD/CAD/CNY procurement from manufacturers in USA, Switzerland, or China, with field 70 referencing the invoice number and commercial contract; (3) irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit (UCP 600) for high-value first-time international reagent purchases, to be opened through Banco Santander or BBVA trade desks, with SWIFT MT700 issuance and payment via MT202/MT103 upon presentation of compliant documents; (4) for LATAM distributor collections, use SWIFT MT103 with EUR or USD settlement under invoice-dated tenor, applying Banco de España customer-reference codes CS/VZ; invoiced proceeds should be net-triangularly routed via a Santander/Banco Bilbao network branch when the LATAM beneficiary has no direct SWIFT relationship with Spain.Outright FX forwards (forward de divisas) up to 12-month tenor for USD/EUR payables-receivables matching, reported under the Bank of Spain BOP statistics.Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-IMF-convertible currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, Chilean peso, BRL) permitted strictly for hedging commercial exposures with physical settlement of the local-leg notional, subject to bank credit approval and CMOF/ISDA master netting.Cross-currency swaps (swaps de divisas) and FX basis swaps for long-duration USD/EUR funding alignment of CAPEX or import financing.FX options and collar structures (OTC plain-vanilla) permissible for strategic USD capex hedging; embedded derivative approval required under MiFID II appropriateness tests.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility: MEDIUM for a Spanish SL in IVD reagent wholesale; PSD2-licensed European e-money institutions (e.g., Wise Business, Qonto, Ramp Network equivalent) may be opened remotely for ancillary payments and multi-currency currency access without a Spanish branch under EEA passporting. Legal constraint: EMIs cannot provide credit, LC operations, or margin FX; inbound payments from LATAM distributors are subject to heightened AML false-positives in the healthcare sector, so the EMI ledger must not be used as the sole collection vehicle; SEPA accountability and the SL's NIF-linked bank account validation still require a traditional deposit-taking entity for capital escrow and treasury concentration.

Stage 06

Corporate Tax & Transfer Pricing

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly incorporated entities may apply a 15% rate during the first tax period in which they obtain a positive taxable base and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish company to non-residents. Domestic Spanish withholding on dividends is also generally 19%. Qualifying distributions to an EU or EEA parent may be exempt under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive implementation where the ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and other statutory conditions are satisfied. Spanish participation exemption rules may reduce taxation at shareholder level but do not automatically eliminate source-country withholding.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 200: within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending 31 December, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202: generally 1 to 20 April, October, and December; electronic payment may require earlier bank cut-off procedures.

Deadline: · Frequency:

Normally 1 to 20 April, October, and December. The final installment is reconciled against Modelo 200.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Spain does not use one universal transaction threshold for all transfer-pricing documentation. Local File documentation is generally required for related-party transactions unless a statutory exemption or simplified documentation rule applies. A commonly relevant exemption applies where the aggregate value of transactions of the same type with the same related party does not exceed EUR 250,000 in the tax period, subject to exclusions including transfers of businesses, shares or participations, real estate, and certain transactions involving intangible assets. Master File documentation is generally relevant where the Spanish entity belongs to a group meeting the EUR 45 million consolidated turnover threshold. Modelo 232 reporting may be required for specified related-party transaction categories and thresholds.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation for ordinary Spanish companies. Substance is nevertheless material under Spanish anti-abuse rules, transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership analysis, the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance framework, controlled foreign company rules, principal-purpose and treaty anti-abuse provisions, and the general anti-avoidance and conflict-in-application doctrines. The SL should maintain Spanish commercial rationale, premises or operational infrastructure where appropriate, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, decision-making records, inventory and logistics evidence, bank-account control, board minutes, and functions-and-risks documentation. A distribution company with no genuine purchasing, inventory, regulatory, customer, or logistics functions may face recharacterization, denial of treaty benefits, or profit-allocation adjustments.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Corporate tax evasion and fraudulent tax reporting

Statutory sanction: Administrative penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on the seriousness of the violation. Where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 for a tax period, criminal tax fraud may arise, generally punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded, with aggravated ranges in specified circumstances.

Director personal liability: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability where they personally participate or act as responsible decision-makers. They may also face subsidiary tax liability for failure to enforce compliance or for causing the company to cease operations without satisfying tax debts. Civil restitution, asset seizure, disqualification, and imprisonment may apply in criminal proceedings. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered by a court where legally justified.
VAT fraud and missing-trader arrangements

Statutory sanction: VAT assessments, repayment of improperly claimed input VAT, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties may apply. Material fraud may trigger criminal tax-fraud charges, asset tracing, seizure, and imprisonment.

Director personal liability: Directors may be criminally liable for knowing participation or deliberate facilitation. Personal tax liability may arise under statutory subsidiary-liability rules where directors cause or permit non-compliance. Courts may impose asset preservation or travel measures in criminal proceedings.
Transfer-pricing manipulation and profit diversion

Statutory sanction: The AEAT may make primary and secondary transfer-pricing adjustments, deny deductions, reclassify payments, assess tax, interest, and specific documentation penalties. Failure to provide required documentation or providing materially incorrect documentation may trigger penalties calculated by reference to data omitted or incorrectly reported, subject to statutory minimums and caps.

Director personal liability: Directors may face personal liability where deliberate manipulation, false records, or abusive conduct is established. Ordinary pricing disagreement does not automatically create criminal liability or pierce the corporate veil.
Beneficial-ownership and treaty-abuse failure

Statutory sanction: Denial of treaty or EU Directive relief, assessment of unwithheld tax, late-payment interest, withholding penalties, and potential anti-abuse or criminal consequences where documents are falsified or the arrangement is fraudulent.

Director personal liability: The Spanish payer and responsible officers may be liable for unpaid withholding tax where statutory conditions are met. Directors may face criminal exposure for falsification, fraud, or deliberate evasion; personal liability is not automatic solely because treaty relief is denied.
Shell company, artificial residency, or effective-management failure

Statutory sanction: The AEAT may challenge Spanish or foreign tax residence, deny deductions or treaty benefits, apply transfer-pricing adjustments, impose tax and interest, and invoke anti-abuse doctrines. Sham transactions may result in administrative penalties or criminal charges.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur personal liability for knowingly maintaining false corporate records or facilitating fraud. Corporate veil piercing requires exceptional proof of abuse, fraud, or unlawful diversion; it is not automatic for low substance or poor governance alone.
Anti-money-laundering and beneficial-owner non-compliance

Statutory sanction: Under Spanish Law 10/2010, serious and very serious AML breaches may attract monetary penalties based on statutory fixed ranges and, in relevant cases, a percentage of annual turnover, together with public reprimands, temporary management restrictions, or disqualification. Criminal money-laundering conduct may result in imprisonment and fines.

Director personal liability: Managers and directors responsible for AML systems may receive personal administrative sanctions and may be criminally prosecuted for knowing participation. Asset freezing and travel restrictions may be ordered in criminal proceedings where proportionate and legally authorized.
Unlicensed or non-compliant distribution of in-vitro diagnostic products

Statutory sanction: Regulatory measures may include product withdrawal, recall, suspension or prohibition of marketing, seizure, administrative fines, and liability for safety-related damage. Tax deductions and customs treatment may also be challenged where commercial documentation is defective.

Director personal liability: Directors and responsible technical personnel may face administrative or criminal liability for deliberate distribution of unsafe or unlawfully marketed products. Civil claims for product damage may extend to the company and, in exceptional cases involving personal misconduct, individuals.
Accounting, corporate-book, and electronic-filing failures

Statutory sanction: Tax assessments, loss of deduction, estimation of taxable income, accounting sanctions, late-filing penalties, possible director disqualification in insolvency proceedings, and increased audit risk may result.

Director personal liability: Directors must act diligently and may be liable for losses caused by intentional or negligent breach of accounting and filing duties. Personal liability and disqualification are particularly relevant where the failure contributes to insolvency or creditor prejudice.
Profit distribution in breach of capital-maintenance rules

Statutory sanction: Invalid or recoverable distributions, shareholder repayment obligations, creditor claims, director damages liability, and potential insolvency-law consequences may apply.

Director personal liability: Directors approving unlawful dividends may be jointly liable for restoration of unlawfully distributed amounts and related damages. Liability is generally civil or insolvency-based; imprisonment requires separate criminal conduct.
